questions.prompt: Why must the pass rule be written in the research log before the test runs?
options: Because the backtest needs it as a parameter
Because a rule chosen after seeing the result can always be bent to fit that result
Because a written rule makes the strategy's t-statistic higher
Because the log file cannot be changed after the first row
questions.explanation: If you pick the bar after seeing the number, you can always pick a bar the number clears. Writing it first means the result can fail.

questions.prompt: Your log shows 20 variants of one idea, and the best has a t-statistic of 2.1. In the simulation, strategies with no edge gave a best t-statistic above 2 in 40% of cases after 20 variants. What should you conclude?
options: The idea is proven, because 2.1 is above 2
The best variant has a 2% chance of being luck
The result is weak evidence, because 20 tries of a strategy with no edge clear 2 in 40% of cases
You should delete the 19 weaker rows and keep the best
questions.explanation: The bar of 2 holds for one test. After 20 tries, luck alone clears it in 40% of cases, so 2.1 says little about a real edge.

questions.prompt: Which row belongs in the research log?
options: Every variant you ran, including the ones that failed
Only variants with a t-statistic above 2
Only the final variant you plan to trade
Only variants that passed the stress tests
questions.explanation: The count of all tries sets how high the bar must be. Leaving out failures makes the best result look rarer, and so more convincing, than it is.
